passage: On the terrace after the society's Diwali party, Rohan dared everyone to climb onto the water-tank ledge for a photo. Gurleen looked at the drop and said, "I'll pass. I'm going to the swings, anyone want chai afterwards?" Somebody muttered, "Boring." She grinned, shrugged, and walked off without another word. A minute later she heard footsteps. Nilesh caught up, hands in his pockets. "I didn't want to either," he said, "but I wasn't going to be the first to say it." She didn't lecture him. She just said, "Race you to the swing?" Later, when the others climbed down laughing and shaking, she waved them over for chai as well, without any comment.

qa.q: Where did Gurleen go when she refused to climb onto the ledge?
How did Nilesh feel about the dare, and why did he follow Gurleen?
qa.a: Nilesh was uneasy about climbing but afraid to be the first to say so, and Gurleen's refusal gave him a way out.

qa.q: What did Gurleen do that kept things friendly after she refused?
qa.a: She said no lightly, didn't lecture Nilesh, and later waved the others over for chai without a comment.

qa.q: How might the others see Gurleen's choice?
qa.a: Some may find it boring, as one muttered. But her cheerful invitation to chai gives them no reason to feel judged, so it may be easier for them to accept it.

grounding: The protagonist refuses peer pressure lightly, another friend follows her, and she stays friendly without preaching.

passage:
"Pankaj, the whole class is bunking to watch the match at Rohit's place. You in?"
"Nah, I'll stay. Maths test tomorrow."
"You're such a nerd, yaar."
"Maybe. Have fun though."
Later, only two of them were left in the classroom.
"Vijay? You stayed too?"
"Yeah. I heard you say no, and I thought… I also don't really want to go."
"Cool. Want to go through the sums together?"
"Okay. But don't lecture me about bunking."
"I wasn't going to. It's your call."
Next morning, the others came in tired, joking about the match.
"Pankaj, you missed the best over ever."
"Tell me about it at lunch."
Vijay whispered, "You're not going to say anything?"
"Why would I? They made their choice. We made ours."
At lunch, Pankaj sat with everyone and listened to the whole match story. Vijay sat next to him, relaxed.

qa.q: What was the class going to watch at Rohit's place?
Why did Vijay stay back after Pankaj said no?
qa.a: Vijay felt relieved and encouraged by Pankaj's refusal, because he didn't really want to go either.

qa.q: What did Pankaj do that made others comfortable?
qa.a: He stayed friendly, didn't lecture Vijay or sneer at those who went, and still listened to their match story at lunch.

qa.q: How might the classmates who bunked see Pankaj the next day?
qa.a: They seem relaxed around him and happy to share the match story, since he doesn't judge them.

grounding: A teen who refuses peer pressure is followed by another, stays friendly and never preaches or sneers at those who went.

passage:
At the mall last winter, my friends dared each other to slip lipsticks into their pockets without paying. "Everyone does it. It's just a game," one of them said.
I said, "Nope, not for me," and walked over to the bookshop. I wasn't trying to be a hero. My stomach was in knots.
A minute later, Lalremsiami followed me in. "I didn't want to either," she whispered. We flipped through comics, pretending to be calm.
Later the others came out giggling, and one of them showed off what she'd taken. I felt a flash of judgement, like I wanted to say, "That's stealing." But I remembered how much I hate being lectured.
So I just said, "Let's get momos," and we all went together. I didn't sneer. Lalremsiami squeezed my arm on the way.
Later that week, one of the girls quietly told me she'd gone back and paid. I never asked her to. I'm Ritu, and I think not preaching helped.

qa.q: Where did Ritu go when the others started the dare?
How did Ritu feel when refusing the dare?
qa.a: Ritu felt nervous, stomach in knots, and not like a hero at all.

qa.q: What did Ritu do that helped, and why?
qa.a: Ritu stayed friendly, suggested momos instead of lecturing, and didn't sneer, which kept the friendship and may have helped a friend choose to pay.

qa.q: How did Lalremsiami feel when she followed Ritu?
qa.a: Lalremsiami felt relieved to have someone else say no, since she didn't want to do the dare either.

grounding: A teen who refuses a shoplifting dare is followed by a friend and stays friendly without preaching or sneering at those who did it.
